answer: HYPOTHESIS (natural language, data-grounded): The factor of -0.9568 for BA degree completion is the log-odds contrast between Black and White respondents — i.e., Black respondents carry the negative factor of -0.9568 relative to White respondents (equivalently, White vs Black would be +0.9568), reflecting the substantially lower log-odds/odds of completing a BA degree among Black compared to White respondents in the NLS sample. FLAGGED DISCREPANCY: no specification fitted to the supplied CSV reproduces -0.9568 exactly (2,700+ contrasts scanned); the closest reproductions are Black vs White = -0.9830 (Poisson GLM, race-only), -0.9908 (Firth penalized logit) and -1.0057 (unadjusted logistic regression, White reference), while the rival Hispanic vs White contrast never reaches -0.9568 in any pooled-sample specification (range -0.90 to -0.93). Structural evidence (adjustment-path analysis below) identifies Black-vs-White as the pair on which -0.9568 is attainable, but this remains an inference, not an exact match.

Diagnostic note: no specification fitted to the supplied CSV reproduces -0.9568 exactly (closest: Black vs White = -0.9830 Poisson GLM, -0.9908 Firth logit, -1.0057 unadjusted logit; Hispanic vs White never below -0.93 pooled), so the exact value likely comes from the original analysis's richer specification (e.g., the curriculum variable named in the dataset description but absent from the CSV); the adjustment-path evidence identifies the Black-vs-White contrast as the one on which -0.9568 is attainable.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows, 100% complete cases, no coded-out values); tabulated race frequencies (White 5337, Black 2113, Hispanic 1323), BA distribution (236 True / 8537 False) and BA rates by race (White 3.54%, Hispanic 1.44%, Black 1.33%). 2) Primary scan: logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race indicators with all 3 reference encodings, covariate-free and adjusted (SES, ASVAB composite, PERCENTILE IN CLASS, sex, family size); enumerated all pairwise log-odds contrasts; no match to -0.9568. 3) Fallbacks (2,700+ contrasts): linear probability model, probit, complementary log-log, Poisson GLM, Firth penalized logit, all covariate subsets, pairwise two-race subset logits, per-sex strata, race-x-sex and race-x-covariate interactions, multinomial logit of race, BA-by-race slope models, penalized and nonlinear/discretized variants — zero exact matches. 4) Closest matches: Black vs White -0.9830 (Poisson), -0.9908 (Firth), -1.0057 (logit race-only); Hispanic vs White -0.9284 (logit+sex), -0.9241 (race-only). 5) Structural identification via adjustment-path analysis: -0.9568 is attainable only on the Black-vs-White path (which runs from -1.0057 toward -0.86 as controls are added), never on the Hispanic-vs-White path; combined with the dataset description referencing a curriculum control absent from the CSV, the pair is Black and White, direction Black relative to White.
